# Education in New Zealand
Education in New Zealand encompasses early childhood education, primary and secondary schooling, and a broad tertiary sector. Early childhood education is delivered in a range of settings (teacher-led kindergartens, Kōhanga Reo, playcentres) and must follow the national curriculum framework, Te Whāriki. Primary and secondary education is compulsory between ages six and sixteen, but most children begin school at age five. Schooling covers Years 1–13, with primary education up to Year 8 and secondary education from Year 9 to Year 13. The system includes state, state-integrated, and private schools, each following curriculum guidelines outlined in the New Zealand Curriculum (NZC) for English-medium schools and Te Marautanga o Aotearoa for Māori-medium schools.
State and state-integrated schools receive government funding, with additional support provided based on student numbers and socio-economic decile ratings. Students may attend Māori-medium education (Kura Kaupapa Māori), and there is a strong emphasis on the revitalization of the Māori language through immersion and subject-based education. From Year 11 onwards, students pursue qualifications primarily through the National Certificate of Educational Achievement (NCEA), with some schools also offering Cambridge International Examinations and the International Baccalaureate. Tertiary education includes universities, polytechnics, and private training establishments. Access to education is supported through government-subsidized student loans and allowances. The sector faces challenges including educational outcomes disparity among Māori and Pacific students and ongoing concerns about literacy, numeracy standards, and school bullying.
